en: Most verbs add -ed for the past: walked, opened.

Stories are told in the past, so learn the most frequent ones first.

Muchos verbos comunes cambian: go → went, see → saw, take → took.
El pasado es igual para todas las personas: I went, she went.
Los cuentos se narran en pasado: aprende primero los más frecuentes.

en: English sentences need a subject, even when Spanish drops it: She is tired.

To say something exists, use there is (one) or there are (more).
In the past: there was, there were: There was a door.

Para clima, hora y distancia usa it: It's raining. It's late.
Para decir que algo existe (hay): there is (uno) o there are (varios).
En pasado (había): there was, there were: There was a door.

title.en: Nobody came: one negative is enough

en: Standard English uses one negative word per idea: I don't see anybody.
With not, use any-: I didn't say anything. She doesn't have any money.
Or use a no- word alone: I said nothing. Nobody came.
Some characters in books use two negatives: that's dialect, not standard English.
es: El inglés estándar usa una sola negación por idea: I don't see anybody.
Con not, usa any-: I didn't say anything. She doesn't have any money.
O usa solo la palabra con no-: I said nothing. Nobody came (no vino nadie).
Algunos personajes usan dos negaciones: es dialecto, no inglés estándar.

en: Question word + helper + subject + verb: Where do you live?

Con be, se invierten el sujeto y be: Where is the key? Is she ready?
Si la palabra interrogativa es el sujeto, no va do: Who opened the door?
Dentro de una oración, orden normal: I don't know where he lives.

title.en: He works: the -s in the present

en: With he, she, it or one person or thing, add -s to the verb: she works.
Add -es after s, sh, ch, x, o: watches, goes. Consonant + y becomes -ies: studies.
have becomes has. Questions and negatives use does + base verb: Does she work?
es: Con he, she, it o una persona o cosa, el verbo lleva -s: she works.
-es después de s, sh, ch, x, o: watches, goes. Consonante + y se vuelve -ies: studies.
have se vuelve has. Preguntas y negativas: does + verbo base: Does she work?

en: The adjective goes before the noun: a red door, an old man.
Adjectives never take -s: red doors, old men.
Noun + noun: the main thing goes last: a kitchen door is a door.
The first noun is usually singular: a shoe shop, a ten-year-old boy.
es: El adjetivo va antes del sustantivo: a red door, an old man.
Los adjetivos nunca llevan -s: red doors, old men.
Sustantivo + sustantivo: lo principal va al final: a kitchen door es una puerta.
El primer sustantivo suele ir en singular: a shoe shop, a ten-year-old boy.
